title: pvSurfaceFlow
body:
## pvSurfaceFlow

Computes the net flux of a point vector field through a surface: at each point it takes the dot product of the vector with a normal averaged from the neighbouring 2-D cells, then integrates it over the surface with Integrate Variables. The output is a one-point unstructured grid whose point array Surface Flow holds the integral (vector units times area), e.g. a volumetric flow rate when the vector is velocity. Use it on a slice, a boundary patch or any 2-D surface; integrate gives other surface integrals.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Only 2-D cells (triangles, quads, polygons, pixels) contribute; feed a surface, not a volume mesh.
- Point normals are made mutually consistent but their overall sign follows the first cell's orientation, so the flux sign may be reversed; check it against a known inflow.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `SurfaceFlow`. Identity: `filters/IntegrateFlowThroughSurface`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Surface Flow filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 3 components. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
